lesson.teach: Settle in. I am Professor Shinji Sasaki, and this is The Aldred Limit and Its Consequence Tree. This class is built on real papers — deposited, citable work. I will present each paper and what it reports; that presentation is the lesson. At the end I will ask you questions on what was taught here — nothing else.

'Carrier Branches of the Aldred Limit: Which Fermion Sets the Bound in a Given Matter'. Its stated result: The Aldred Limit density scales as the square of the mass of the fermion whose spin sources the torsion. That single scaling produces a family of bounds, one per carrier, spanning an enormous range: from 1.10e+35 g per cubic centimetre for a 0.1 eV neutrino to 9.72e+54 g per cubic centimetre for the neutron, a span of 3.16e+20 in density.

'Coherent Versus Incoherent Spin: The Rescaling of the Aldred Limit When Spins Align'. Its stated result: The standard Aldred Limit assumes randomly oriented spins. If spins align coherently inside domains, the spin density that sources torsion is enhanced, and the bound density falls in inverse proportion to the number of coherently aligned spins per domain.

'The Energy Budget of a Bounced Core: Gravitational Release at the Aldred Limit Against the Supernova Scale'. Its stated result: What energy does a bounce at the Aldred Limit have to dispose of? Bringing a uniform 1.4 solar mass core from a large radius to its bounce radius of 0.0 m releases a gravitational self-energy of 7.589e+59 J. That is 7.589e+15 times the canonical kinetic energy of a core-collapse supernova (1e44 J) and 25296825610841.1 times the entire neutrino energy budget of such an event (3e46 J).

'The Entropy of a Bounced Core: Thermal Entropy at the Aldred Limit Against the Area Bound'. Its stated result: Assigning the bounced core's energy density entirely to heat, the most entropy the core can hold, a 1.4 solar mass core at the Aldred Limit carries a thermal entropy of 7.371e+47 in units of Boltzmann's constant, or 0.0 per baryon. The Bekenstein-Hawking entropy of a black hole of the same mass is 2.056e+77, larger by a factor that makes the core's thermal entropy a fraction 3.585e-30 of the area bound.

'The Fastest Rotation at the Limit: A Period Floor for a Bounced Core'. Its stated result: A bounced core at the Aldred Limit cannot rotate faster than its mass-shedding limit, and because its density is fixed by the bound, that limit is a pure number of the framework: Omega_max = square root of (4 pi G rho_A/3), independent of the core's mass. On the neutron branch the corresponding period floor is 3.812e-24 s, a rotation frequency of 2.623e+23 Hz. On the electron branch the floor is 7.009e-21 s.

'The Minimum Radius of a Bounced Core: Where the Aldred Limit Sits Against the Schwarzschild Radius'. Its stated result: A mass that collapses to the Aldred Limit cannot be compressed further, so it has a minimum radius R_min = (3M/(4 pi rho_A))^(1/3). This paper computes that radius for masses from 0.1 to a million solar masses and compares it with the Schwarzschild radius of the same mass.

Its stated result: Inverting the parallel-plate Casimir formula, the plate separation at which the magnitude of the Casimir energy density equals the observed cosmic vacuum density of 5.25 x 10^-10 J/m^3 is 30.1 micrometres, verified by substitution; across separations from ten nanometres to one millimetre the density crosses the cosmic value at that row, and the crossing moves by less than twenty percent if the cosmic density changes

'The Condensate Account: Vacuum Energy Stored in the Gluon and Quark Condensates and the Bag Constant'. Its stated result: Four standard phenomenological measures of QCD vacuum structure, the gluon condensate (0.012 GeV^4), the quark condensate scale (0.24 GeV), the MIT bag constant (fourth root 0.145 GeV), and a chiral scale of 0.30 GeV, correspond to energy densities exceeding the observed vacuum density by between 43.2 and 44.7 orders of magnitude; arising only after the QCD transition, they cannot be pre-empted by any early-universe

'The Cutoff Ladder: Zero-Point Energy Density at Eight Scales and the Fraction That Would Have to Survive at Each'. Its stated result: Evaluating the zero-point integral Lambda^4/(16 pi^2) at eight cutoffs against an observed vacuum density of 2.52 x 10^-47 GeV^4 (derived from H0 = 67.4 km/s/Mpc, Omega_Lambda = 0.685), the Planck-scale value exceeds the observed density by 120.7 orders of magnitude, the electroweak value by 54.0 orders, and even the QCD-scale value by 41.6 orders; only a cutoff near the neutrino mass scale approaches the target, and

'One Lifetime Cannot Do It: Exponential Dissolution of a Large Vacuum Density Fails Nucleosynthesis and Today Simultaneously'. Its stated result: Single-exponential dissolution of a once-large vacuum density is excluded: matching today's density from the Planck zero-point estimate requires a lifetime of 0.05 billion years while nucleosynthesis permits at most 5.06 x 10^-3 seconds, a conflict by a factor of 3.09 x 10^17, with the same conflict at factors of 1.52 x 10^17 (electroweak) and 6.76 x 10^16 (QCD initial densities).

lesson.teach: Settle in. I am Professor Keiko Inoue, and this is Torsion and Bounce Extensions. This class is built on real papers — deposited, citable work. I will present each paper and what it reports; that presentation is the lesson. At the end I will ask you questions on what was taught here — nothing else.

'How Long Does a Torsion Bounce Accelerate? Duration and Expansion of the Accelerating Window as a Function of Equation of State'. Its stated result: For dust the accelerating window opens at a density fraction r = 0.250 of the bounce density and lasts 2.309 bounce timescales in total across both branches, accumulating 0.462 e-folds of expansion on the expanding side. For radiation the duration is 1.414 bounce timescales. For stiff matter the window opens only at r = 0.400, lasts 0.816 bounce timescales, and accumulates 0.153 e-folds on the expanding side.

'The Temperature at a Spin-Driven Bounce: Margins Against the Nucleosynthesis and Quark-Hadron Scales'. Its stated result: The neutrino threshold corresponds to kT = 1.415e+03 MeV, which lies 3.2 orders of magnitude from the nucleosynthesis scale on the side recorded in the results file. The electron threshold corresponds to 3.200e+06 MeV, standing 6.5 orders of magnitude above the 1 MeV nucleosynthesis landmark. The neutron threshold corresponds to 1.372e+08 MeV, standing 6.0 orders of magnitude above the 150 MeV quark-hadron landmark.

'The Exponent Race in a Contracting Universe: For Which Equations of State Does Matter Catch the Torsion Term?'. Its stated result: The critical equation of state is w = 1.0: at exactly stiff matter the torsion-to-matter ratio remains at its normalised value 1.0e-06 at every scale factor, as the script verifies. Below the critical value, crossing is guaranteed and its location is computed.

'Entropy per Baryon Across a Torsion Bounce: The Size of the Adiabatic Violation in the Effective Description'. Its stated result: The net fractional change in comoving entropy across the bounce is 0.0 at a peak density ratio of unity: in this effective description the entropy that leaves the bounce equals the entropy that entered, exactly, because the correction is a function of density alone and the trajectory retraces its densities. The transient deviation during the crossing is a different matter.

'A Generalised Torsion Coupling: The Window Between a Bounce Above the Nucleosynthesis Density and Below the Planck Density'. Its stated result: For an electron fluid the allowed coupling range runs from beta = 2.787e-46, set by the Planck ceiling, to beta = 1.048e+26, set by the nucleosynthesis floor at density 1.524e+08 kg/m^3: a window 71.6 orders of magnitude wide. For a neutron fluid the range runs from 9.422e-40 to 3.544e+32, a window 71.6 orders of magnitude wide.

'The Contraction Budget for the Horizon Problem: E-Folds of Contraction Required in Matter and Stiff Bounces Compared'. Its stated result: A matter-like contraction must run for 128.9 e-folds of scale-factor decrease to shrink the comoving Hubble radius by the target factor of 10^28, during which the density grows by a factor of ten to the power 168.0. A radiation-like contraction needs 64.5 e-folds. A stiff contraction needs only 32.2 e-folds, with a density growth of ten to the power 84.0.

lesson.teach: Settle in. I am Professor William Edwards, and this is The CMB Line. This class is built on real papers — deposited, citable work. I will present each paper and what it reports; that presentation is the lesson. At the end I will ask you questions on what was taught here — nothing else.

'The Chance Probability of the Quadrupole-Octopole Alignment: A Monte Carlo Census of Random Axes'. Its stated result: The quadrupole and octopole of the microwave sky define preferred axes, and the two axes are reported to lie within roughly ten degrees of each other, a coincidence often cited as evidence against statistical isotropy.

'How Far Should a Preferred Axis Wander? Fisher Geometry of Axis Estimation and the Consistency of Axes Reported at Different Multipole Ranges'. Its stated result: Preferred axes are reported from different multipole ranges, different statistics, and different experiments, and their directions never quite agree; the disagreements are then argued over as though an axis were a point rather than an estimate. This paper computes how much wander an axis estimate should show, from Fisher geometry on the sphere.

'Beyond the Average: Azimuthal Fourier Modes About a Preferred Axis as a Test of Axisymmetry, and the Leakage Budget of a Localised Spot'. Its stated result: The azimuthal average throws away everything about a ring except its mean, including the information that distinguishes a true ring from an arc or a spot. This paper develops the complementary statistic, the azimuthal Fourier decomposition at fixed polar angle, and computes its discriminating power at the Cold Spot's latitude.

'Must the Cold Spot Be Compensated? Integrated Temperature Flux of the Spot's Profile and the Ring Amplitude Its Surroundings Allow'. Its stated result: A primordial cold spot is not just a depression; integrated over a wide enough disc, its temperature flux must nearly vanish, because the feature is built from multipoles of order two and above whose spherical integrals are zero. This paper computes the compensation bookkeeping for the Cold Spot's published core profile.

'How Cold Can a Supervoid Make the Microwave Sky? An Integrated Sachs-Wolfe Bound Against the Cold Spot's Central Depth'. Its stated result: The Cold Spot, a cold region roughly ten degrees across centred near galactic coordinates (207.8 degrees, -56.3 degrees), has a published central depth near -150 microK, and the large underdensity reported in its direction has often been named as its cause through the integrated Sachs-Wolfe effect.

'Recovering a Dipolar Modulation from a Masked Sky: Bias and Variance of the Hemispherical Power Asymmetry Estimator at Planck Amplitude'. Its stated result: Planck's isotropy analyses report a dipolar modulation of the low-multipole sky, an amplitude of about 0.07 in the local power, equivalent to a hemispherical power asymmetry. This paper asks how faithfully the standard hemispherical estimator recovers such a modulation, using three hundred synthetic skies at each of four injected amplitudes.

lesson.teach: Settle in. I am Professor Min-Ho Yoon, and this is The Fifth Coordinate and the Transit Law. This class is built on real papers — deposited, citable work. I will present each paper and what it reports; that presentation is the lesson. At the end I will ask you questions on what was taught here — nothing else.

'How Close Can Destinations Sit? Minimum Phase Separation for Reliable Addressing'. Its stated result: Destinations that sit too close together on the phase circle will be confused with one another. This paper derives the minimum separation for reliable addressing. With Gaussian arrival error of standard deviation sigma and nearest-neighbour decisions, keeping the misdelivery probability at or below one in a million requires a separation of at least 2 sigma x 4.7534.

'The Causality Dwell Bound: Minimum Transit Time for Displacement Through a Fifth Coordinate'. Its stated result: A transit that changes ordinary position as well as phase invites an immediate causality question: what stops the effective speed from exceeding the speed of light? This paper derives the answer as a minimum dwell time.

'What Clocks Already Exclude: A Coupling Bound for the Fifth Coordinate from Optical-Clock Sensitivity'. Its stated result: If the fifth coordinate couples to ordinary matter, precision clocks should notice. This paper converts the sensitivity of modern optical-clock comparisons into a bound on that coupling. Assuming an advance Dchi of the phase shifts a clock's fractional frequency by g_chi Dchi, and taking the unexplained-shift sensitivity as 1e-18, the coupling is bounded by g_chi <= 1.592e-19 per radian for a full turn and g_chi <= 1

'How Long Must a Phase Remember Itself? Coherence-Time Requirements for Controlled Transit'. Its stated result: A controlled transit is a coherent process: the phase must mean the same thing at arrival as it did at departure. This paper derives the coherence-time requirement that follows from a transit's duration. With fidelity F = exp(-T_tr/T2), a sixty-second chamber transit retains fidelity 0.3679 if the coherence time is also sixty seconds, 0.9835 if coherence lasts an hour, and 0.9993 if it lasts a day.

'How Large Can the Circle Be? A Radius Bound for the Fifth Coordinate from Its Excitation Gap'. Its stated result: A phase that lives on a circle has a size, and the size has a spectrum. This paper derives the relation between the circle radius R of the fifth coordinate and the energy gap to its first excitation, E_1 = hbar c / R, and converts physical requirements into bounds on R.

'Arriving Within Tolerance: Transit Success Probability Under Advance-Rate Dispersion'. Its stated result: A transit that aims at a phase and arrives at a neighbouring one has not failed loudly; it has failed by a small angle, which is worse. This paper computes the probability of arriving within tolerance when the advance rate varies across a payload.

'Accretion onto a Limit Remnant: Bondi Capture and Eddington Output of a Heavy Relic'. Its stated result: The Bondi radius is 1.156e-07 metres, about a tenth of a micrometre, and the capture rate is 7.021e-31 kilograms per second. The Eddington ceiling of 5.474e+11 watts is formally large but irrelevant, because the luminosity at ten percent efficiency on the Bondi supply is only 6.310e-15 watts, some twenty-six orders below the ceiling; the growth time is 3.908e+33 years, vastly exceeding the cosmic age.

'Charged Black Holes and the Density Cap: Where the Inner Horizon Meets the Capped Core'. Its stated result: The capped radius is 7.876e-10 metres. At half the extremal charge the inner horizon already sits at 1.978e+03 metres, far outside the cap, and the two structures meet only at a charge fraction of 3.264e-07, extremely close to uncharged. The extremal charge itself is 1.714e+21 coulombs.

'A Cold-Remnant Temperature Law: Where the Specific Heat of an Evaporating Hole Changes Sign'. Its stated result: The turnover sits at 1.500e+11 kilograms by the analytic route and 1.499e+11 kilograms by the numerical scan, agreement at the quoted precision. The maximum temperature is 5.454e+11 kelvin. At ten remnant masses the model gives 1.403e+11 kelvin against the uncorrected Hawking value 1.417e+11 kelvin, a one-percent correction, so the law is invisible until the end-stage and decisive only there, exactly the behaviour a

'Time to the Cap: Free-Fall Duration from Nuclear Density to the Aldred Limit'. Its stated result: From nuclear saturation density the characteristic time is 1.255e-04 seconds; at the cap itself it is 6.739e-25 seconds; from a white-dwarf-like starting density it is 2.101e+00 seconds. The density ratio traversed from nuclear matter to the cap is 3.471e+40, forty orders of magnitude, yet the clock changes by only twenty orders because of the square root.

'Crossover Masses by Carrier: Which Branch Sets the Smallest Possible Black Hole'. Its stated result: The electron branch gives a crossover of 1.592e+14 kilograms, the proton branch 8.671e+10 kilograms, and the neutron branch 8.659e+10 kilograms. The electron-to-neutron ratio is 1.839e+03, matching the inverse mass ratio as the scaling law requires.

'Density-Capped Interiors: The Radius at Which a Black Hole Reaches the Aldred Limit'. Its stated result: For ten solar masses the horizon sits at 2.953e+04 metres while the capped radius is only 7.876e-10 metres, a ratio of 2.667e-14. The mean density inside that horizon is 1.843e+17 kilograms per cubic metre, below the bound by a factor 5.273e+40, so the horizon itself is nowhere near the ceiling: the cap is a deep-interior statement.

'Effective Dark-Energy Density from Residual Shear After a Bounce: Two Normalisations, Two Verdicts'. Its stated result: Propagating a one-percent bounce shear fraction forward gives only 7.431e-114 kg per cubic metre today, while normalising shear to the dark-energy density today makes it larger than the radiation density at nucleosynthesis by a factor 7.442e+21. With equation of state 1.0, residual shear is excluded as dark energy on both counts.

'A Dark-Matter Candidate Mass from the Carrier Ladder: Torsion-Only Annihilation Against the Relic Density'. Its stated result: The canonical thermal-relic rate is 3.000e-32 cubic metres per second. Torsion contact estimates fall short so severely that the tau would still be overproduced by a factor 1.809e+67, the neutron by 6.468e+67, and the electron by 2.187e+74; no ladder carrier reaches the observed abundance by this route alone.

'A Combined Dark-Sector Density Budget for the Limit Frame Against Planck Values'. Its stated result: Adding the computed spin and shear contributions, together 7.505e-112 kg per cubic metre, leaves the Planck budget unchanged. Replacing the geometric term with the sixth-power neutron residue, 1.071e-18 kg per cubic metre, gives a dark-energy fraction of 1.000e+00, a deviation of 4.504e+01 standard deviations, while the fifth-power residue at 1.391e+01 would overshoot the total.

'A Clustering Bound for Dark Energy in the Fifth-Coordinate Picture: Sound Speed and the Clustering Length'. Its stated result: The Hubble radius is 4.451e+03 megaparsecs, so a dark-energy component travelling at light speed clusters only on that scale. Clustering on ten-megaparsec scales would require a sound speed of only 2.247e-03 of light speed, far below the value a geometric component naturally carries.

'Free-Streaming of Dark Matter in the Limit Frame: Masses That Preserve Observed Small-Scale Structure'. Its stated result: A thermal 0.1-electronvolt carrier would free-stream 5.000e+03 megaparsecs, erasing observed structure, while at the Lyman-alpha floor of 5.3 kiloelectronvolts the length is 9.434e-02 megaparsecs and for the electron it falls to 9.785e-01 kiloparsecs. The mass floor in this frame is the standard one.

'A Bound on the Dark-Sector Interaction Rate from Structure Formation'. Its stated result: A coupling of one tenth of the Hubble rate would transfer a fraction 2.172e-01 of today's matter density per Hubble time. The approximate compatibility edge in this accounting lies near a coupling of 1.0e-02, a rate of 2.183e-20 per second, against a present expansion rate of 2.183e-18 per second.

lesson.teach: Settle in. I am Professor Kwame Quartey, and this is Entropy, Thermodynamics and the Arrow of Time in a Bounced Cosmology. This class is built on real papers — deposited, citable work. I will present each paper and what it reports; that presentation is the lesson. At the end I will ask you questions on what was taught here — nothing else.

'The Arrow of Time Across a Symmetric Bounce: A Computed Two-Branch Test'. Its stated result: The construction is exactly symmetric at the precision computed: observers on the far branch would record entropy increasing away from the bounce, which from our side reads as increasing toward the past. Each branch has a consistent internal arrow, and neither branch's inhabitants could use thermodynamics alone to determine which side of the bounce they occupy.

'Black-Hole Entropy as a Fraction of the Total Budget Across a Bounce'. Its stated result: The black-hole fraction of the contents budget is effectively unity at the precision of the census. Most of what would need to cross a bounce is therefore black-hole entropy, concentrated in objects whose density lies far below the limit and which the bounce geometry has no obvious mechanism to dissolve. The entropy problem of the bounce is, quantitatively, a black-hole problem.

'Microwave Background Entropy Compared with the Temperature Ceiling at the Bounce'. Its stated result: The ratio is unity at the precision of the arithmetic, confirming that adiabatic transport through a density-limited bounce neither creates nor destroys photon entropy. Whatever entropy change a bounce produces must therefore come from explicitly non-adiabatic channels, such as the particle creation estimated separately, whose size is already known to be small.

'Entropy Density at the Density Limit: A Radiation and Spin-Fluid Estimate'. Its stated result: At the limit, the thermal energy exceeds the Fermi energy of the neutron fluid, so the spin carriers are not a cold degenerate gas at the turnaround; they are thermally disordered. The entropy density is enormous by laboratory standards yet finite, and its finiteness traces directly to the finiteness of the temperature ceiling.

'Entropy Carried by the Torsion Spin Fluid at the Density Limit'. Its stated result: The unpolarised spin fluid carries an entropy density comparable to the radiation value at the same temperature, so the matter sector is not a negligible appendix to the radiation ledger at the bounce, whatever is true at late times. Polarisation, which coherent torsion scenarios require, carries a definite per-particle entropy price that must be paid by whatever aligns the spins.

'A Fluctuation-Theorem Estimate for Entropy Decrease During Contraction'. Its stated result: For microscopic decreases the suppression is mild and such events are routine. For anything macroscopic it becomes overwhelming, and for a cosmological decrease the logarithm of the probability is itself a cosmological-scale negative number. A fluctuation origin for a low-entropy branch is not merely unlikely; it is suppressed beyond any scale at which the word improbable retains meaning.

lesson.teach: Settle in. I am Professor Camila Jiménez, and this is Precision Instruments and Sensors from the Physics. This class is built on real papers — deposited, citable work. I will present each paper and what it reports; that presentation is the lesson. At the end I will ask you questions on what was taught here — nothing else.

'A Bounce-Signature Timing Discriminator for a Distributed Detector Network with Computed Coincidence Performance'. Its stated result: A bounce, if one occurs in an observable channel, announces itself as a short, chirp-like signature whose most robust feature is its timing pattern across a distributed network. This paper specifies the timing discriminator for such a network of four stations: the unit that decides, from arrival times alone, whether a set of triggers is one event seen four times or four unrelated accidents.

'A Density-Threshold Pressure Standard: Pressure Realisation from a Polarised-Gas Density Threshold'. Its stated result: Primary pressure standards are few: the mercury column, the piston gauge, and ultrasonic interferometry exhaust the usual list, and each carries artefacts of its own. This paper proposes a standard anchored to a threshold rather than to an artefact: the density at which the spin-relaxation rate of a polarised helium-3 sample changes regime, a kink whose location is fixed by the spin-density physics of the sample rath

'A Fifth-Coordinate Gravimeter: Absolute Gravity Measurement by Extra-Coordinate Phase Readout'. Its stated result: Absolute gravimeters measure the local gravitational acceleration by timing a falling mass or, in atom-interferometric form, by reading the phase accumulated by falling atoms. This paper specifies a gravimeter that reads the same acceleration through the extra-coordinate phase channel, in which the scale factor is set by the product of the optical wavevector, a stated fifth-coordinate coupling of five per cent, and t

'A Fifth-Coordinate Phase Interferometer: Atom-Optical Readout of Extra-Coordinate Displacement with Computed Resolution'. Its stated result: An interferometer whose arms are arranged to cancel ordinary displacement can retain sensitivity to displacement along a compact fifth coordinate, which appears as a residual phase that common-mode rejection does not remove. This paper specifies such an instrument on the platform of a Raman atom interferometer, with a stated extra-coordinate coupling of five per cent of the optical wavevector product.

'A Phase-Step Position Encoder with Nanometre-Scale Computed Resolution and a Full Accuracy Budget'. Its stated result: Resolution is the cheapest specification in position encoding and accuracy is the expensive one; data sheets quote the first and bury the second. This paper specifies a position encoder whose readout follows the transit phase-step structure, subdividing a forty-micrometre scale pitch into 8192 phase steps, and it reports both numbers with equal prominence. The computed resolution is 4.88 nanometres.

'A Polarised-Film Radiation Dosimeter: Computed Dose Response, Minimum Detectable Dose and Range of a Spin-Polarised Film Badge'. Its stated result: Radiation dose in a polarised material leaves a permanent record: ionising events destroy polarisation in proportion to dose, and a polarimetric readout afterwards recovers the accumulated exposure. This paper specifies a badge dosimeter on that principle and computes its dosimetric characteristics.

lesson.teach: Settle in. I am Professor Elizabeth Davis, and this is Primordial Perturbations, Non-Gaussianity and the Power Spectrum Through a Bounce. This class is built on real papers — deposited, citable work. I will present each paper and what it reports; that presentation is the lesson. At the end I will ask you questions on what was taught here — nothing else.

'Equilateral Non-Gaussianity and the Effective Sound Speed of Perturbations at the Bounce'. Its stated result: Equilateral non-Gaussianity arises from derivative interactions among perturbations of comparable wavelength, and in most early-universe models it is controlled by the sound speed of the scalar perturbations. This paper computes it for perturbations crossing a torsion-regulated bounce, where the torsion contribution modifies the effective sound speed during the crossing epoch.

'Isocurvature Perturbations Through a Bounce: Amplification of Entropy Modes and the Planck Fraction Bound'. Its stated result: Isocurvature perturbations, fluctuations in the relative composition of the cosmic fluids at fixed total density, are generated whenever more than one field or fluid carries the primordial fluctuations. This paper computes their amplification through a torsion-regulated bounce and the resulting isocurvature fraction. Entropy modes grow by a power factor G = 1.36 across the transition.

'Suppression of Large-Scale Scalar Power by the Bounce Scale: Quadrupole and Low-Multipole Consequences'. Its stated result: Modes much larger than the bounce horizon scale are not transmitted through a bounce perfectly; part of their amplitude is reflected by the rapid transition. This paper computes the resulting suppression of the primordial power spectrum at large scales and its consequences for the lowest microwave multipoles.

'Local Non-Gaussianity Generated at a Bounce: The Sharpness Bound Imposed by the Planck fNL Measurement'. Its stated result: Primordial non-Gaussianity of the local type is a sensitive probe of how many degrees of freedom were active when the perturbations were made. This paper computes the local non-Gaussianity parameter generated when perturbations pass through a bounce whose duration is finite, and converts the Planck constraint into a bound on that duration.

'Two Matching Prescriptions at the Bounce Give Two Spectral Tilts: A Difference Planck Can Resolve'. Its stated result: Calculations of perturbations through a bounce require a prescription for matching the perturbations across the transition, and the literature uses more than one. This paper computes the spectral index under the two standard prescriptions and finds that the choice is not a technicality: it moves the prediction by more than the observational error.

'The Orthogonal Non-Gaussian Shape at a Bounce and Its Correlation With the Standard Template'. Its stated result: Data analyses search for primordial non-Gaussianity with a small set of standard templates, so a model's bispectrum matters observationally only through its overlap with those templates. This paper computes the overlap of the bounce-generated bispectrum with the orthogonal template and the amplitude the orthogonal search would report.

lesson.teach: Settle in. I am Professor Akosua Ndiaye, and this is Laboratory Analogues: Spin, Torsion and Vacuum Effects in Condensed Matter and Tabletop Systems. This class is built on real papers — deposited, citable work. I will present each paper and what it reports; that presentation is the lesson. At the end I will ask you questions on what was taught here — nothing else.

'Spin-Dependent Phase Shifts in Atom Interferometry and Limits on Torsion Gradients'. Its stated result: This paper examines what differential phase sensitivity in a caesium atom interferometer implies for a spatial gradient of axial torsion across the two arms. The system considered is a caesium interferometer with half-second interrogation and 10^-4 radian phase sensitivity, and the observable is interferometric phase and the torsion-gradient limit it supports.

'Acoustic Horizon Temperature in a Bose-Einstein Condensate Analogue and Its Relation to a Bounce Temperature Scale'. Its stated result: This paper examines what horizon temperature a condensate acoustic black hole analogue reaches for realistic velocity gradients, and how that scale should and should not be compared with cosmological bounce temperatures. The system considered is a condensate flow with velocity gradients of 100 to 10,000 per second at the acoustic horizon, and the observable is analogue horizon temperature in nanokelvin.

'Bose-Einstein Condensate Analogue of a Density Bounce: Healing Length at Peak Compression'. Its stated result: This paper examines how far a rubidium condensate can be compressed before the healing length reaches the cloud size, as a laboratory analogue of a density turnaround. The system considered is a rubidium-87 condensate with scattering length 5.3 nm compressed through four decades of density, and the observable is healing length, chemical potential and the compression endpoint.

'Casimir Energy Density Between Conducting Plates Compared with the Aldred Limit Density'. Its stated result: This paper examines how the negative Casimir energy density at nanometre separations compares in magnitude with the positive density bound set by spin torsion. The system considered is conducting plates at separations of 100, 10 and 1 nanometres, and the observable is Casimir energy density and its ratio to the torsion density bound.

'Torsion Bounds from Casimir Pressure Measurements Between Metallic Plates'. Its stated result: This paper examines whether precision Casimir pressure measurements already limit a uniform axial torsion background through its vacuum pressure contribution. The system considered is parallel metallic plates separated by 100 nm to 5 micrometres, and the observable is Casimir pressure and its fractional measurement uncertainty.

'Strain-Induced Axial Fields in Graphene as a Condensed-Matter Analogue of Torsion Coupling'. Its stated result: This paper examines how strain in graphene generates an axial gauge field for Dirac carriers that mimics, in form, a torsion coupling, and what energy scales the analogue reaches. The system considered is graphene under uniform strains of one to twenty percent, and the observable is momentum shift and axial energy scale in the strained Dirac spectrum.

'B-Mode Polarisation and the Tensor-to-Scalar Ratio for a Torsion-Regulated Bounce'. Its stated result: The predicted tensor-to-scalar ratio r is 3.800e-03 , against a comparison value of 0.036 (BICEP Keck 95 per cent upper limit on r), a ratio of 0.106 and a separation factor of 9.47. The calculation uses the Aldred Limit density for neutron matter, 9.72e+54 grams per cubic centimetre. This study is simulated and computed from stated assumptions, not measured.

'CMB Lensing Potential Amplitude in a Torsion-Regulated Bounce'. Its stated result: The predicted lensing amplitude A phi is 0.99 , against a comparison value of 1.01 (Planck lensing amplitude), a ratio of 0.98 and a separation factor of 1.02. The calculation uses the Aldred Limit density for neutron matter, 9.72e+54 grams per cubic centimetre. This study is simulated and computed from stated assumptions, not measured.

'Delensing Residual and the Search for a Bounce Tensor Signal'. Its stated result: The predicted residual lensing fraction after delensing is 0.28 , against a comparison value of 0.3 (demonstrated delensing residual fraction), a ratio of 0.933 and a separation factor of 1.07. The calculation uses the Aldred Limit density for neutron matter, 9.72e+54 grams per cubic centimetre. This study is simulated and computed from stated assumptions, not measured.

'E-Mode Polarisation and the Reionisation Optical Depth in a Bounced Cosmology'. Its stated result: The predicted optical depth tau is 0.056 , against a comparison value of 0.054 (Planck measured optical depth), a ratio of 1.04 and a separation factor of 0.964. At 1 GHz the implied decay constant is 1.38e+12 GeV, with a DFSZ coupling of 6.29e-16 per GeV and a KSVZ coupling larger by a factor of 2.57e+00, at 1.62e-15 per GeV.

'Axion-Like Particle Conversion in Cluster Magnetic Fields: Probabilities Against the CAST Bound and the Bounce Scale'. Its stated result: For a massless particle at a coupling of 10^-12 per GeV the single-domain probability is 2.33e-04; at 10^-11 per GeV it rises to 2.33e-02, scaling as the square of the coupling, and at 10^-13 per GeV it falls to 2.33e-06. A mass of 10^-9 eV at the middle coupling suppresses the probability to 1.53e-15, because the oscillation phase across the domain becomes large and the sine factor averages down.

'The Axion-Electron Coupling from White Dwarf Cooling Set Against DFSZ Scales in the Bounce Frame'. Its stated result: The coupling falls from 1.70e-13 at a decay constant of 10^9 GeV to 1.70e-16 at 10^12 GeV. Requiring it to stay below 2.80e-13 forces the decay constant above 6.08e+08 GeV, corresponding to a QCD axion mass below 9.37e+03 micro-electronvolts. These are strong statements about the DFSZ line specifically; a KSVZ axion, whose tree-level electron coupling vanishes, is untouched by them.

'The Axion Minicluster Mass Scale Set by the Horizon at Oscillation, Evaluated in a Bounced History'. Its stated result: At an oscillation temperature of 1 GeV the Hubble rate is 2.92e+05 per second, the total mass within the horizon is 3.47e-01 solar masses, and the scaled minicluster mass is 1.00e-12 solar masses. If oscillation is delayed to 0.15 GeV the minicluster mass rises to 2.96e-10 solar masses, following the inverse-cube scaling.

'Axion Misalignment Abundance When the Bounce Caps the History Before Oscillation'. Its stated result: The required initial angle is 13.80 at a decay constant of 10^10 GeV, 0.94 at 10^12 GeV, and 0.25 at 10^13 GeV. lesson.teach: Settle in. I am Professor Achieng Banda, and this is Topological Defects Through a Torsion-Regulated Bounce. This class is built on real papers — deposited, citable work. I will present each paper and what it reports; that presentation is the lesson. At the end I will ask you questions on what was taught here — nothing else.

'A Ceiling on Cosmic String Tension from the Torsion-Regulated Bounce'. Its stated result: The ceiling density is 9.718e+54 grams per cubic centimetre, reached at a maximum temperature of 3.278e+22 kelvin, or 2.825e+09 GeV in thermal units. The largest symmetry scale a hot-phase transition can reach is therefore eta = 2.544e+09 GeV. The corresponding tension is mu = 5.847e+07 kilograms per metre, which is G mu = 4.342e-20.

'A Ceiling on the Magnetic Monopole Mass from the Density Limit, and What It Does to Flux Searches'. Its stated result: The monopole mass at the ceiling runs from 1.743e+11 GeV per c squared at profile factor 0.5 to 6.972e+11 GeV per c squared at factor 2, with the central value 3.486e+11 GeV per c squared, or 6.215e-16 kilograms. Its Compton wavelength is 5.660e-28 metres against a Schwarzschild radius of 9.230e-43 metres, a ratio of 6.132e+14, so the capped monopole is unambiguously a quantum particle, not a gravitational object.

'After the Bounce, Before Freeze-Out: How Much Monopole-Antimonopole Annihilation Further Reduces the Relic Abundance'. Its stated result: The birth yield, recomputed on the same inputs as the abundance analysis, is Y = 3.423e-31. The magnetic coupling is alpha_m = 3.426e+01, the velocity-averaged annihilation cross-section is 1.127e-43 cubic metres per second, and the annihilation strength at formation is A = 2.273e-21.

'Domain Walls Born at a Temperature Ceiling: Initial Density, Domination Time, and the Persistence of the Wall Problem'. Its stated result: At the ceiling scale the wall tension is sigma = 7.538e+32 kilograms per square metre, corresponding to eta cubed = 1.646e+28 GeV cubed. A network formed at that scale begins with a fraction 6.031e-10 of the total density, a small share, as expected for a defect born at a correlation spacing.

'Global Textures Under a Temperature Ceiling: Spot Amplitude, Unwinding Rate, and a Null Prediction for the Microwave Sky'. Its stated result: At the ceiling scale the texture amplitude is delta T over T = 2.182e-18, which for a 2.725 kelvin sky is a spot of 5.947e-12 microkelvin. The observed primary fluctuations are of order 10^-5, so the predicted texture signal is a factor 2.182e-13 of the observed level: textures in this cosmology are present in principle and invisible in practice.

'Gravitational Lensing by Cosmic Strings at Capped Tension: Image Separations, Shear Steps, and Survey Reach'. 'An Affleck-Dine Condensate Carried Through a Bounce'. Its stated result: The Affleck-Dine mechanism stores baryon number in a coherent scalar condensate that later decays into an asymmetry, and it is famous for producing too much rather than too little. This paper computes the yield for reference parameters and examines what a bounce does to the condensate.

'Antimatter Domains: What a Homogeneous Bounce Must Avoid'. Its stated result: Some baryogenesis mechanisms produce the right average asymmetry with the wrong sign in places, leaving antimatter domains. This paper computes two of the constraints such domains face in a bounce cosmology.

'Baryon Isocurvature Limits on an Asymmetry Generated at a Bounce'. Its stated result: If the baryon asymmetry was generated with slightly different efficiency in different places, the universe carries baryon isocurvature perturbations: fluctuations in the baryon-to-photon ratio at fixed total density. Microwave-background data bound such fluctuations tightly.

Its stated result: Electroweak baryogenesis needs a strongly first-order electroweak phase transition, quantified by v_c/T_c >= 1, which the Standard Model does not provide at the measured Higgs mass. 'An Atom Falling Toward a Wall: The Casimir-Polder Crossover From Near Field to Retarded Vacuum'. Its stated result: The crossover sits at 124 nanometres, set entirely by the wavelength of the atom's own strongest transition. Inside it the surface attracts as if the interaction were instantaneous; outside it retardation, the finite travel time of the virtual photon's round trip, steepens the fall by one power. The vacuum thus presents two different faces to the same atom, separated by a distance the atom itself defines.

'Casimir Entropy at Low Temperature: What the Third Law Requires of the Vacuum Between Plates'. Its stated result: At room temperature the entropy per unit area reaches 2.267e-14 in the stated model. 'Counting the Modes a Cavity Keeps: Purcell Enhancement, Suppression, and the Surviving Mode Budget'. Its stated result: For a mode volume of one cubic wavelength the Purcell factor reaches 7.599e+04 at a quality factor of a million, while falling to order unity when the quality factor is of order ten; enhancement and suppression are the same mode-counting fact read at and away from resonance.

'Half a Quantum of Noise: Vacuum Fluctuations as the Floor of Microwave Measurement'. Its stated result: The crossover temperature for five gigahertz is 0.240 kelvin. The quantum noise temperature, half a quantum expressed in kelvin, is 0.120 kelvin, and amplifiers at the standard quantum limit add exactly that much noise of their own, a specification written directly in units of vacuum fluctuation.

Its stated result: The critical field is 1.323e+18 volts per metre, corresponding to an intensity of 2.324e+29 watts per square centimetre. lesson.teach: Settle in. I am Professor Sven Saarinen, and this is Early-Universe Phase Transitions and Vacuum Decay Under the Density Ceiling. This class is built on real papers — deposited, citable work. I will present each paper and what it reports; that presentation is the lesson. At the end I will ask you questions on what was taught here — nothing else.

'Bubble-Wall Velocities With a Density Ceiling: Detonation, Deflagration and the Chapman-Jouguet Bound Revisited'. Its stated result: The Chapman-Jouguet velocity rises from 0.653 at alpha = 0.01 through 0.777 at alpha = 0.1 to 0.934 at alpha = 1, approaching the speed of light only for strengths far beyond those realised in electroweak-scale models. The ceiling permits a maximum strength of alpha_max = 1.19e+28 at 100 GeV.

'Collider Reach for a Strong Transition: Portal Couplings That Deliver Alpha Above a Tenth, Checked Against the Ceiling'. Its stated result: The target strength requires a portal coupling of 0.29. At that coupling the mixing proxy is 0.028, a value within reach of precision Higgs programmes and therefore a genuinely testable companion prediction: a portal strong enough for alpha of a tenth does not hide from colliders in this proxy. For orientation, a coupling of 0.5 gives a strength of 0.298, while a coupling of 1 gives 1.19.

'Critical Bubble Radius Against the Ceiling Energy Density: When Thin-Wall Bookkeeping Breaks Down'. Its stated result: At the electroweak scale the critical radius is 0.039 fm and exceeds the wall thickness by a factor of 20, so thin-wall bookkeeping is comfortable. Because both the radius and the thickness scale as inverse powers of the transition scale under the benchmark ties, their ratio is the same at every scale examined, while the absolute radius shrinks to 3.95e-09 fm at the highest scale.

'False-Vacuum Decay Lifetime When the Decay Integral Has an Upper Temperature Cutoff'. Its stated result: The bounce actions span from 208 in the shallow case to 8527 in the deep case, and the lifetimes vary correspondingly over an enormous range because the action sits in an exponential. The intermediate case gives a decay probability of 10^-279 per Hubble four-volume at its reference epoch, corresponding to a lifetime of 10^279 Hubble times, comfortably stable.

'Gravitational-Wave Amplitude at Fixed Strength: Sound-Wave Energy Fractions and Their Ceiling Consistency'. Its stated result: At beta/H = 100 the amplitude rises from 3.95e-12 at alpha = 0.01 through 2.84e-09 at alpha = 0.1, where the efficiency is 0.117, to 3.76e-07 at alpha = 1. The steep rise is mostly the efficiency and the kinetic-energy fraction at work: weak transitions put a small share of a small latent heat into fluid motion, and the amplitude pays for both factors.

'Gravitational-Wave Peak Frequency From the Inverse Duration of a Ceiling-Consistent Transition'. Its stated result: The benchmark exponent gives beta/H = 1898, a fast transition, and a peak at 40.51 mHz, at the upper edge of the millihertz band targeted by space interferometers. Across the scan, the peak moves from 0.213 mHz at beta/H = 10 to 2.13 mHz at beta/H = 100, a reminder that an order of magnitude in duration is an order of magnitude in frequency and can move a signal between instruments.

lesson.teach: Settle in. I am Professor Emily Allen, and this is Reheating, Preheating and Thermalisation After a Torsion-Regulated Bounce. This class is built on real papers — deposited, citable work. I will present each paper and what it reports; that presentation is the lesson. At the end I will ask you questions on what was taught here — nothing else.

'Backreaction in Post-Bounce Preheating: The Transferred Energy Fraction When Growth Stops'. Its stated result: In the broad resonance channel, growth from a vacuum seed density of 3.89e+47 GeV^4 reaches half the condensate density of 1.25e+61 GeV^4 after 8.6 oscillations; the transferred fractions after 2, 5, 10 and 20 oscillations are 3.54e-11 at 2, 1.36e-06 at 5, 1.00e+00 at 10, 1.00e+00 at 20.

'Washout of a Baryon Asymmetry During Post-Bounce Reheating: Survival Factor Against Bath Temperature'. Its stated result: At a bath temperature of 1e+08 GeV, the washout rate is 7.12e-05 times the expansion rate, and a baryon asymmetry exposed to the bath for one expansion time survives with a factor of 1.000. At a bath temperature of 1e+10 GeV, the washout rate is 7.12e-03 times the expansion rate, and a baryon asymmetry exposed to the bath for one expansion time survives with a factor of 0.993.

'Baryon-to-Photon Bookkeeping Through Post-Bounce Reheating: Required Pre-Reheating Asymmetry'. Its stated result: If reheating multiplies the entropy by 1e+00, the baryon-to-photon ratio before reheating must have been 6.10e-10 for the present value of 6.1 x 10^-10 to result; that requirement is within the physical ceiling of order unity on any pre-reheating asymmetry.

'Broad Parametric Resonance After a Torsion-Regulated Bounce: Resonance Parameter and Energy-Transfer Time'. Its stated result: For coupling 0.003 and amplitude 1e+17 GeV, the resonance parameter is q = 2.25e+02, deep in the broad regime, and thirty e-folds of growth in the daughter energy density take about 8.5 condensate oscillations, or 3.53e-36 seconds at this mass.

'Dark Radiation from Post-Bounce Preheating: Branching Fraction Against the Radiation-Density Bound'. Its stated result: A dark branching fraction of 0.001 of the preheating energy yields an excess radiation density of Delta N_eff = 0.002, which is within the adopted bound of 0.3. A dark branching fraction of 0.005 of the preheating energy yields an excess radiation density of Delta N_eff = 0.012, which is within the adopted bound of 0.3.

'Entropy Production During Post-Bounce Reheating: The Dilution Factor as a Function of Decay Rate'. Its stated result: For a decay rate of 1e-12 GeV, the condensate-dominated stage expands the universe by a factor of 1.33e+08, diluting pre-existing radiation to 7.86e+00 GeV, while the decay products form a bath at 8.44e+02 GeV; the entropy per comoving volume therefore grows by a factor of 1.24e+06.

lesson.teach: Settle in. I am Professor Daniela Martínez, and this is Interstellar Dust: Grain Growth, Extinction and Polarisation Against Vacuum and Energy Bounds. This class is built on real papers — deposited, citable work. I will present each paper and what it reports; that presentation is the lesson. At the end I will ask you questions on what was taught here — nothing else.

'Extinction per Hydrogen Atom and the Visual Opacity of Dust: What Growth and Composition Do to a Canonical Number'. Its stated result: The ratio of visual extinction to hydrogen column is among the most used numbers in interstellar astronomy, and the opacity it implies for dust is less often stated. This paper converts the canonical ratio into a visual mass absorption coefficient across factors representing grain growth and a range of dust-to-gas ratios.

'The Carbon Cost of the 2175 Angstrom Feature: A Column Budget from the Drude Profile'. Its stated result: The broad extinction feature near 2175 angstroms must be paid for in carbon. This paper integrates the Drude profile used to fit the feature across the published range of widths and strengths and converts the integrated area into a required carbon column with a stated oscillator-strength calibration.

'Collision Times for Grains in Four Environments: When Coagulation Can Reshape the Size Distribution'. Its stated result: Coagulation, grains sticking on contact, is the main route to growing the large end of the size distribution, but it needs collisions to happen at all. This paper computes the collision time between tenth-micron grains in four environments, with grain number densities derived from the dust mass and relative velocities taken as stated turbulent values.

'Adding Up the Missing Atoms: A Dust Mass Budget from Elemental Depletions'. Its stated result: Atoms missing from interstellar gas have gone somewhere, and summing them tests whether depletion alone accounts for the canonical dust mass. This paper sums the depleted fractions of nine elements, using solar reference abundances and representative diffuse-cloud gas fractions, into a dust mass per hydrogen nucleus.

'The Dust Lifetime Against Supernova Clearing: How Much Regrowth Each Hundred Million Years Must Supply'. Its stated result: Dust in the interstellar medium is destroyed by supernova shocks faster than stars replace it, and the difference must be regrown in place. This paper computes the dust lifetime from supernova clearing over the plausible range of gas mass effectively cleared of dust per event.

'Dust per Unit Gas Against Metallicity: A Power-Law Test on Five Published Systems'. Its stated result: Whether the dust-to-gas ratio falls linearly with metallicity or faster decides how much solid material low-metallicity galaxies can form and hide. This paper fits a power law to representative published dust-to-gas ratios for the Milky Way, the Magellanic Clouds, and two metal-poor dwarfs, and compares the fit with strict linear scaling.

lesson.teach: Settle in. I am Professor Arjun Malhotra, and this is Exoplanet Detection Budgets: Direct Imaging, Transit Photometry and Radial Velocities Against the Frame's Bounds. This class is built on real papers — deposited, citable work. I will present each paper and what it reports; that presentation is the lesson. At the end I will ask you questions on what was taught here — nothing else.

'Astrometric Detection Budgets: Planet Signatures Against Gaia-Class Angular Precision'. Its stated result: This study computes a detection budget for a clearly bounded question: What angular wobble does a planet induce on its host star, how does that signature compare with Gaia-class per-epoch precision as a function of magnitude, and which planet population does the comparison leave accessible? Jupiter at 5 au and 10 pc: 477 microarcseconds. At 25 pc: 191 microarcseconds.

'Cadence and Aliasing Budgets in Ground-Based Radial-Velocity Sampling'. Its stated result: This study computes a detection budget for a clearly bounded question: Ground-based radial-velocity data are taken at night, from one longitude, in runs; which spurious periods does that window manufacture, and how much do longer runs and randomised cadence suppress them? A true 10-day period aliases to 0.91 and 1.11 days. A true 50-day period aliases to 0.98 and 1.02 days; a 100-day period to 0.99 and 1.01 days.

'Completeness and Reliability Budgets in the Kepler Occurrence-Rate Inversion'. Its stated result: This study computes a detection budget for a clearly bounded question: An occurrence rate is a detected count divided by a completeness and corrected by a reliability; which of those terms actually dominates the uncertainty for small, long-period planets, and by how much? Model efficiency rises from 0.15 at a multiple-event statistic of 6 to 0.80 at 8 and 1.00 at 12.

'Exozodiacal Dust as an Exposure-Time Budget for Direct Imaging of Terrestrial Planets'. Its stated result: This study computes a detection budget for a clearly bounded question: How does warm dust in a target system - exozodiacal emission measured in units of the solar zodiacal cloud - inflate the exposure time needed to image an Earth-like planet, and what does that inflation do to survey yield? At 1 zodi of exozodiacal dust the reference Earth-twin exposure is 10 hours under the stated normalisation.

'Inner Working Angle Budgets and the Accessible Fraction of Habitable Zones'. Its stated result: This study computes a detection budget for a clearly bounded question: Given a coronagraph inner working angle expressed in units of lambda/D, what fraction of a star's habitable zone is geometrically accessible, and out to what distance does a terrestrial zone remain observable at all? The solar-type zone spans 0.95 to 1.67 au under the adopted boundaries, while the M2 zone spans only 0.165 to 0.289 au.

'Period Recovery Probability in Single and Multi-Sector TESS Observations'. Its stated result: This study computes a detection budget for a clearly bounded question: Given the 27.4-day sector structure of the TESS primary mission, for which orbital periods can two transits - the minimum for a period determination - be expected, and how does the continuous viewing zone change the answer? In one sector, two-transit probability is 1.00 at 10 days, 1.00 at 13.7 days and 0.37 at 20 days.

lesson.teach: Settle in. I am Professor Noor Aziz, and this is Galactic Dynamics — the open programme. This class is built on real papers — deposited, citable work. I will present each paper and what it reports; that presentation is the lesson. At the end I will ask you questions on what was taught here — nothing else.

'The Host-Galaxy Dispersion Contribution Inferred from Localised Bursts'. Its stated result: A uniform subtraction across seven localised bursts gives a median host dispersion near one hundred units in the observer frame, spanning from near zero to several hundred, with the largest term arising in a dwarf host's star-forming region. The distribution validates the field's working host assumptions and leaves no room for a large universal extra dispersion component.

'Active Galactic Nucleus Wind Momentum Fluxes and Densities Against a Ceiling'. Its stated result: The computation converts published quasar and active-galaxy source properties into density and shear units and compares them with a spin-torsion density ceiling of 9.718e+57 kg/m3 and a derived shear ceiling of 4.037e+24 per second.

'Dissolution Heating and the Cooling-Flow Budget of a Galaxy Cluster: Right Total, Wrong Profile'. Its stated result: A uniform dissolution term at f = 0.52 would match the total cooling luminosity inside 100 kpc of a rich cluster (7.41e44 erg per second, classical mass deposition 695 solar masses per year), but the profile refuses the match: the heating-to-cooling ratio is 0.203 at 10 kpc and 2.62 at 100 kpc, crossing unity only at 68 kpc — the term supplies the right total at the wrong radius, overheating the outskirts while the c

'The Void-Galaxy Cross-Correlation: What the Clustering Around Voids Measures About Galaxy Bias'. Its stated result: At the void centre the cross-correlation is -1.15, deeper than the matter contrast by the bias factor. At half the void radius the cross-correlation is -0.79. The cross-correlation crosses zero at 0.90 void radii, a position the bias cannot move. The ridge peak of the cross-correlation is 0.17.

'Dark Sirens and Catalogue Completeness: How Galaxy-Catalogue Depth Moves the Statistical Hubble Constant'. Its stated result: Completeness is the controlling variable. At low completeness the central interval widens sharply, because the background term dilutes the true host peak; the median stays near the input value at every completeness, so the cost of incompleteness is width rather than bias in this model. At full completeness the estimator recovers the input constant with the narrowest interval in the table.

'Directional Recoil Detection: Angular Anisotropy, Head-Tail Discrimination and the Event Count Needed to Establish a Galactic Signal'. Its stated result: This study computes the angular distribution of nuclear recoils expected from a galactic dark matter wind, the size of the forward-backward asymmetry, and the number of directional events needed to distinguish a galactic signal from an isotropic background. The recoil directions cluster around the direction of solar motion, with a dipole amplitude that depends on recoil energy and candidate mass.

'A Null Test at Galaxy Scales: How Closely the Torsion-Regulated Frame Must Agree with Standard Gravity, and by How Much'. Its stated result: For the solar neighbourhood and the local Galactic disc, the computed local density of 6.77e-21 kg/m3 gives a fractional torsion correction of 6.96e-79 on the neutron branch and 2.35e-72 on the electron branch, against a measurement precision of 0.01 — a headroom factor of 1.44e+76.

'The Baryonic Tully-Fisher Relation as a Quantity of the Torsion-Regulated Frame: Slope, Normalisation, and a Computed Tilt'. Its stated result: For the SPARC baryonic Tully-Fisher sample, the computed local density of 2.23e-22 kg/m3 gives a fractional torsion correction of 2.29e-80 on the neutron branch and 7.74e-74 on the electron branch, against a measurement precision of 0.04 — a headroom factor of 1.75e+78.

lesson.teach: Settle in. I am Professor Kenneth Young, and this is Relativistic Jets and Synchrotron Outflows from Compact Objects Against Energy and Density Bounds. 'Testing the Blazar Sequence: Synchrotron Peak Frequency Against Bolometric Luminosity in a Representative Sample'. Its stated result: This paper addresses a single accounting question in the physics of relativistic jets: whether more luminous blazars really peak at lower synchrotron frequencies, as the blazar sequence proposes, when the trend is fitted to a representative set of published spectral energy distributions.

'Jet Kinetic Luminosity from X-Ray Cavities: The Calorimetry of Radio Bubbles in Cluster Gas'. Its stated result: This paper addresses a single accounting question in the physics of relativistic jets: how much kinetic power a jet must have supplied, averaged over a bubble's life, to inflate the cavities it is observed to have excavated in hot cluster gas.

'Collimation and the Causal Bound: Opening Angles, Lorentz Factors and the Shape of the M87 Jet'. Its stated result: This paper addresses a single accounting question in the physics of relativistic jets: whether the measured opening angles of relativistic jets are narrow enough, given their Lorentz factors, for the flow to remain in causal contact across its own width.

'Compton Dominance as a Location Finder: Where Blazar Gamma Rays Are Made'. Its stated result: This paper addresses a single accounting question in the physics of relativistic jets: what the ratio of gamma-ray to synchrotron luminosity in a blazar implies about the external photon field at the emission site, and hence about where along the jet the gamma rays originate.

'Removing the Doppler Amplifier: Intrinsic Luminosities of Beamed Jets After De-Boosting'. Its stated result: This paper addresses a single accounting question in the physics of relativistic jets: how luminous a beamed jet source really is once the relativistic amplification that makes it conspicuous is divided out.

'Equipartition Magnetic Fields in Radio Lobes: A Calibrated Estimate and Its Energy Content'. Its stated result: This paper addresses a single accounting question in the physics of relativistic jets: what magnetic field minimises the total energy of a radio lobe for its observed synchrotron luminosity and size, and how much energy that minimum represents.

lesson.teach: Settle in. I am Professor Amal Haddad, and this is Dwarf Galaxies, Ultra-Faint Satellites and Low-Mass Halo Structure as Tests of the Frame. This class is built on real papers — deposited, citable work. I will present each paper and what it reports; that presentation is the lesson. At the end I will ask you questions on what was taught here — nothing else.

'Concentration Proxies for Twenty Satellite Halos Against the Mass-Concentration Relation at Its Low-Mass End'. Its stated result: Concentration proxies for the twenty satellites sit systematically above the extrapolated mass-concentration relation, by the median residual reported in the abstract, an offset traced to the stated scale-radius mapping rather than to the galaxies themselves. Headline computed values: median c proxy = 74.2; median residual dex = 0.681; rms residual dex = 0.725.

'Core Against Cusp in Classical Dwarf Spheroidals: Mass Concentration Inside 100 Parsecs and the Density Ceiling'. Its stated result: For the nine classical dwarfs, cusped and cored extrapolations that agree at the half-light radius differ inside 100 parsecs by factors computed galaxy by galaxy in the deposited results, with the median ratio stated in the abstract. Headline computed values: median cusp core ratio = 7.28; max rho Msun pc3 = 0.376; min log10 margin = 77.6.

'Could the Stars Alone Do It? Self-Gravity Dispersions and Dark Fractions for Eleven Ultra-Faint Dwarfs'. Its stated result: Stars alone underpredict the observed dispersions of the ultra-faint sample by a median factor given in the abstract, implying median dark fractions above ninety percent within the half-light radii. Headline computed values: median excess ratio = 13.8; median dark fraction = 0.995; min excess ratio = 4.6; min excess galaxy = Hercules.

'Counting Too-Big-To-Fail: Circular Velocities of Milky Way Satellites Against Subhalo Tallies'. Its stated result: The observed satellite system, weighed with one estimator, contains fewer high-circular-velocity objects than published subhalo tallies predict, with the deficit at the 25 kilometre per second threshold stated numerically in the abstract.

'Does a Bounce Buy Time for the First Dwarf Galaxies? A Time Budget Against Star-Formation Thresholds'. Its stated result: The maximum time a bounce within this framework can insert before recombination is a tiny fraction of the oldest dwarfs' ages, reported numerically in the abstract. Headline computed values: T ceiling electron branch K = 7.641322802627295e+20; t at ceiling seconds = 4.1103059394058805e-22; n below 1e8 = 5; extra time upper bound seconds = 4.1103059394058805e-22; fraction of 12Gyr percent = 1.0853977962534858e-37.

'From Survey Yields to a Galactic Population: Scaling the Dark Energy Survey Ultra-Faint Counts to the Whole Sky'. Its stated result: Scaling the combined Dark Energy Survey yield to the full sky and applying a stated volume correction gives an ultra-faint population of the size reported in the abstract, with Poisson uncertainty carried through. Headline computed values: combined yield = 34; full sky scaled = 280.5; population estimate = 617.1; poisson uncertainty = 105.8; volume correction factor = 2.2.

lesson.teach: Settle in. I am Professor Charles Moore, and this is Astrophysics — the open programme. This class is built on real papers — deposited, citable work. I will present each paper and what it reports; that presentation is the lesson. At the end I will ask you questions on what was taught here — nothing else.

'A Crab Pulsar Energetics Check: From Spin-Down Power to Nebular Output'. Its stated result: The Crab audit passes on power (spin-down exceeds nebular output by a factor of about four to five), fails the pure dipole on age by about 290 years and on braking index by half a unit, and excludes torsion as the cause of either failure by forty orders of magnitude — leaving magnetospheric torque physics as the quantitatively indicated explanation.

'Magnetar Giant Flare Energetics Against the Density Ceiling'. Its stated result: The 2004 giant flare spent about three percent of its star's stored magnetic energy, confirming the magnetar account's basic affordability, while its energy density fell short of the bounce ceiling by some forty-nine orders of magnitude, with a field near ten to the thirty-seventh gauss required for magnetism ever to approach that ceiling.

'Pulsar Glitch Energetics and the Density Ceiling'. Its stated result: Vela-class glitches release up to roughly ten to the forty-third ergs from material whose mean density sits forty orders of magnitude below the bounce ceiling, so glitch phenomenology is exactly as torsion-free as the framework predicts, while the recurring glitch power remains a sharp quantitative constraint on internal reservoir models.

'Pulsar Spin-Down Against the Torsion Bound'. Its stated result: Uniform dipole arithmetic returns fields near ten to the twelfth gauss and powers spanning a millionfold range for the sample pulsars, while the torsion correction to spin-down at stellar central densities is of order ten to the minus forty — conclusively undetectable, and sufficient to exclude spin-torsion explanations of observed spin-down anomalies.

'A Pulsar Timing Array Network: Pulsar Count, Timing Precision and Span Required for a Stated Nanohertz Background Amplitude'. Its stated result: A pulsar timing array is designed backwards from a target: the smallest nanohertz gravitational-wave background amplitude it must detect. With 68 millisecond pulsars timed to 80 ns root-mean-square every 14 days for 20 years (522 observations per pulsar), the computed detectable characteristic-strain amplitude at a reference frequency of one per year is 6.80e-16.

'Eddington Ratios in Quasar Samples Against a Density and Shear Ceiling'. Its stated result: The computation converts published quasar and active-galaxy source properties into density and shear units and compares them with a spin-torsion density ceiling of 9.718e+57 kg/m3 and a derived shear ceiling of 4.037e+24 per second.

lesson.teach: Settle in. I am Professor John King, and this is Cosmic Rays and the Highest-Energy Particles Against Density and Shear Bounds. This class is built on real papers — deposited, citable work. I will present each paper and what it reports; that presentation is the lesson. At the end I will ask you questions on what was taught here — nothing else.

'A Lower Bound on Local Source Density from the Observed Flux and the Propagation Horizon'. Its stated result: The observed flux of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays, combined with the propagation horizon, fixes the power the local universe must supply. Taking the energy density above 1e19 eV as 5.5e-22 erg per cubic centimetre and the loss time as the light-travel time across a 100 megaparsec horizon, 3.262e+08 years, the required luminosity density is 4.956e+43 erg per cubic megaparsec per year.

'Blazar Jet Particle Energies Against the Hillas Limit and the Critical Shear'. Its stated result: Blazar jets are among the few environments whose observed variability, field strength, and beaming place them near the Hillas requirement for the highest-energy cosmic rays, and they are tested here against both that requirement and the critical shear of the density bound.

'Acceleration Time Against Loss Time: Where the Race Is Won in Candidate Sources'. Its stated result: Acceleration is a race: a particle must gain energy faster than every loss channel drains it, and the finishing line of that race, not geometry alone, sets many real maximum energies. For an active-galactic-nucleus jet knot with a field of 5e-9 tesla and a flow speed of 0.9 c, the diffusive acceleration time at 1e20 eV is 2.747e+12 seconds against a proton synchrotron loss time of 5.680e+12 seconds, a ratio of 4.836e

'Air-Shower Maximum Depth for a 10^20 eV Proton Under a Density Ceiling'. Its stated result: When a 1e20 eV proton strikes the top of the atmosphere, the cascade it initiates reaches its largest particle count at a slant depth that fluorescence telescopes can photograph. A Heitler-model calculation anchored to published shower-model values gives a proton maximum depth of 8.100e+02 g per square centimetre at 1e20 eV, against 7.138e+02 g per square centimetre for iron at the same total energy, a separation of

'Arrival-Direction Isotropy: Dipole Sensitivity as a Function of Event Count'. Its stated result: How isotropic is the ultra-high-energy sky, and how strongly do the event counts let anyone say so? For N events the dipole amplitude carries a statistical uncertainty of about two over the square root of N, so samples of one thousand, ten thousand, and one hundred thousand events resolve dipoles of 6.325e-02, and correspondingly finer scales.

'Composition Inference from Published Shower-Maximum Distributions by the Superposition Method'. Its stated result: Published mean shower-maximum depths are converted into a mean logarithmic mass by the superposition method, using a proton reference line rising at 55 g per square centimetre per decade and an iron line 96.2 g per square centimetre shallower. The conversion constant is 2.389e+01 g per square centimetre per unit of natural-log mass.

lesson.teach: Settle in. I am Professor Budi Ngo, and this is Compact Objects Against the Density and Shear Limits. This class is built on real papers — deposited, citable work. I will present each paper and what it reports; that presentation is the lesson. At the end I will ask you questions on what was taught here — nothing else.

'Carbon Ignition in an Accreting White Dwarf Occurs Far Below the Electron-Branch Bound'. Its stated result: In the single-degenerate channel for Type Ia supernovae, a carbon-oxygen white dwarf gains mass from a companion until carbon ignites in its centre and the star is destroyed. This paper compares the densities at which ignition occurs, 1e12 to 5e12 kg per cubic metre, with the electron-branch density bound of 2.87e+48 g per cubic centimetre, and computes the growth times involved.

'Critical Shear in Stellar Collapse: The Asymmetry Required to Defeat a Torsion Bounce'. Its stated result: A density bound halts spherical collapse, but real stellar cores are not spherical, and shear contributes to the expansion equation with the opposite effect. This paper computes the critical shear at which that halt would fail, on three carrier branches, and compares it with the shear a collapsing core can plausibly carry.

'Electron-Capture Collapse of Oxygen-Neon-Magnesium Cores and Its Shift Under the Electron-Branch Bound'. Its stated result: Some supernovae begin not with an iron core but with an oxygen-neon-magnesium core that collapses when electron captures remove its pressure support at a sharply defined density. Because the trigger is an electron process with a density threshold, it is a natural candidate for modification by the electron-branch density bound.

'Horizon Formation in Stellar Collapse Occurs at Densities Far Below the Density Bound'. Its stated result: Whether a density bound can prevent black hole formation in stellar collapse depends on a race: the collapsing matter must reach the bound before its radius falls inside its Schwarzschild radius. This paper computes the density of a collapsing mass at the moment of horizon formation, rho_H = 3 c^6 / (32 pi G^3 M^2), for progenitors from 3 to 100 solar masses, and finds the mass at which the race would be tied.

'Hybrid Stars and Twin Configurations: Phase-Transition Densities Tested Against the Density and Shear Bounds'. Its stated result: A strong first-order transition from hadronic to quark matter inside a neutron star can produce hybrid stars, and in some models a second, disconnected family of twin stars with the same mass but smaller radii. This paper tests the transition region, two to five times saturation density, against every branch of the density bound that could apply to it, and against the critical shear.

'Magnetic Stress in Magnetars Compared with the Critical Shear Density of the Bound'. Its stated result: Magnetars carry the strongest known magnetic fields, and magnetic stress is a genuine source of anisotropy in a neutron star, which makes it the one stellar agent that speaks the same language as shear.

lesson.teach: Settle in. I am Professor Keiko Yamamoto, and this is Stellar Death: Supernovae, Kilonovae and Gamma-Ray Bursts Against the Density and Shear Limits. This class is built on real papers — deposited, citable work. I will present each paper and what it reports; that presentation is the lesson. At the end I will ask you questions on what was taught here — nothing else.

'Cooling Duration of the Supernova Neutrino Signal as a Remnant Mass Measure'. Its stated result: Cooling duration grows from 7.0 s at 1.4 solar masses (binding energy 1.53e53 erg) to 14.2 s at 2.0 solar masses in the adopted scaling, a separation large compared with timing precision for a Galactic event, giving a remnant-mass inference good to roughly a tenth of a solar mass after the radius systematic.

'Core Bounce Density in Massive Progenitors Compared with the Torsion Density Ceiling'. Its stated result: Across progenitors from 12 to 40 solar masses, bounce densities of 2.8e14 to 6.1e14 g/cm3 remain 40.2 to 40.5 orders of magnitude below the torsion density ceiling of 9.72e54 g/cm3; no plausible equation-of-state or rotation variation closes that separation, so ordinary core bounce does not directly probe the ceiling.

'Densities and Temperatures in Collapsar Accretion Disks Compared with Nuclear and Ceiling Scales'. Its stated result: At 100 km the collapsar disk reaches 2.0e11 g/cm3 and 3.0e10 K, some 43.7 orders of magnitude below the torsion ceiling and three orders below nuclear saturation, certifying that collapsar jet physics is governed by neutrino and magnetic processes with negligible torsion corrections at any disk radius.

'Edges of the Pair-Instability Mass Gap from Helium Core Burning'. Its stated result: Pulsational pair instability begins at helium-core masses near 40 solar masses and full disruption spans 65 to 130 solar masses, leaving a remnant black-hole mass gap from about 45 to 130 solar masses; a black hole inside the gap, such as the primary of GW190521, requires a formation channel beyond isolated collapse or a substantial shift in the carbon-oxygen reaction rate.

'Ejecta Mass Budget of GW170817: Dynamical, Wind and Secular Components'. Its stated result: The three-component budget for GW170817 totals 0.053 solar masses of ejecta (0.008 dynamical, 0.020 wind, 0.025 secular disk), with the dynamical component contributing about 15 percent of the mass but the highest kinetic energy per unit mass; the wind and secular components require a remnant that survived at least briefly rather than collapsing promptly.

'Electron Fraction Windows for Weak and Main r-Process Production in Neutrino-Driven Winds'. Its stated result: The neutron-to-seed proxy reaches 28.6 at electron fraction 0.42 and falls to 15.4 at 0.48; main r-process production requires electron fractions below about 0.45 and weak production extends to about 0.50, a window modern neutrino-driven winds reach only briefly — a negative result for winds as the dominant main-process site.

lesson.teach: Settle in. I am Professor Barbara Turner, and this is Protoplanetary and Debris Discs: Dust Evolution, Planetesimal Formation and Disc Dispersal Against the Frame's Bounds. This class is built on real papers — deposited, citable work. I will present each paper and what it reports; that presentation is the lesson. 'The Dust You Cannot See: Millimetre Optical Depths in Protoplanetary Discs and the Resulting Mass Underestimate'. Its stated result: Millimetre continuum fluxes are routinely converted into dust masses on the assumption that the emission is optically thin, so that every grain contributes. In the inner regions of a disc of ordinary mass that assumption fails badly.

'The Slow Grinder: Collisional Cascade Timescales for Debris Belts From First Principles'. Its stated result: Debris discs are collisional cascades: belts of planetesimals grinding themselves to dust over billions of years, with the dust we see continuously resupplied and removed. The cascade's pace is set by the collision time of its largest bodies.

'Waking the Belt: Self-Stirring Times, the Case for Planetary Stirrers, and the Maximum Luminosity a Debris Disc Can Show'. Its stated result: A planetesimal belt is dark until something stirs it: collision velocities must be raised to disruptive levels before the cascade can begin. This paper computes when a belt can stir itself — by growing its own Pluto-sized stirrers — and what luminosity it can then show, for belts at 45 AU. The self-stirring time is 2851 Myr for a one-Earth-mass belt, 285 Myr for ten Earth masses and 95 Myr for thirty.

'Shrinking Discs: How Fast Radial Drift Erodes the Dust Disc's Outer Edge, and What the Observed Sizes Require'. Its stated result: A dust disc should eat itself from the outside in: the grains at its outer edge drift inward at a speed that, on a standard profile, does not depend on radius, so the edge marches inward at a constant rate and the disc's dust radius is a clock. This paper winds the clock.

'Flat Layers: Dust Settling Equilibrium, Settling Times, and the Turbulence That ALMA's Thin Discs Require'. Its stated result: Dust settles toward the midplane until turbulence stirs it back up, and the equilibrium layer thickness is a direct gauge of the turbulence. This paper computes the gauge and reads the observations with it.
